Frequently Asked Questions

This page answers common questions about compressing images to a target size in KB, including how to compress image to 20KB, 100KB and 200KB, which formats work, how quality and dimensions interact, and how your images are handled. Use the search box to filter the questions, or browse the categories below. If you cannot find what you need, read how the tool works for more detail on the method and its limits.

Try the 20KB tool, the 100KB tool or the image resizer.

Using the tool

How do I compress an image to 20KB?

Open the Compress to 20KB tool, add your image, keep the 20KB preset, and download the result when processing finishes. If the status says "above target", try JPEG/WebP output or a smaller maximum width.

How do I compress an image to 100KB?

Open the Compress to 100KB tool, add your image and download the result. Most photos fit after a modest quality reduction or resize.

Why is my image still larger than 20KB?

The tool stops at its quality and size limits to avoid an unusable image, then returns the smallest result and labels it above target. Reduce the maximum width or lower the minimum quality.

Can I compress several images at once?

Yes. Each file is processed with its own status and you can download a ZIP of successful results.

Can I resize an image as well as compress it?

Yes. Open Advanced settings and set a maximum width and/or height. Aspect ratio is preserved and images are never enlarged.

How do I download my compressed image?

Use the Download button on each result, or "Download all (ZIP)" for several files.

How do I compress an image to 200KB?

Open the 200KB tool, add your image and download the result. The 200KB target is roomy, so most photos keep their detail with only a modest reduction. If you need more or less, use the custom size box.

Will my image be accepted by every form?

Not necessarily. Portals set their own rules about size, format and pixel dimensions, and some count 1KB as 1,000 bytes. This site uses 1,024 bytes per KB, so leave a little headroom if a limit is strict, and always read the form's instructions.

General

Can I compress an image online for free?

Yes. The tool is free to use and needs no account.

Can I use the tool on my phone?

Yes. The layout is responsive. Very large photos may be slow or hit memory limits on older phones.

What does KB mean?

Kilobyte. This site uses 1 KB = 1,024 bytes.

How is ImageTo20KB different from Squoosh?

Squoosh is an open-source image compression app from Google Chrome Labs that gives you manual control over codecs and settings. ImageTo20KB focuses on reaching a target size in KB: you enter the size and it searches for the best fit. We are not affiliated with Squoosh, and each suits a different need.

Is there a limit on file size?

Yes. Files above 50 MB or 50 megapixels are rejected to protect your browser from running out of memory. Very large photos may also be slow on older phones.

Privacy

Can I compress an image without uploading it?

Yes. Decoding, resizing and encoding happen in your browser. Your image is not sent to a server for compression.

Does ImageTo20KB store my images?

No server-side storage of images is built into the tool because images are processed locally. Your browser holds them in memory until you remove them or close the page.

Formats

Which image formats are supported?

JPG/JPEG, PNG and WebP input. Output can be JPEG, WebP or PNG depending on your browser. Animated GIF/WebP/APNG, SVG and HEIC are not supported.

Can I compress JPG to 20KB?

Usually yes for small or simple images. Large, detailed photos may need a smaller maximum width. The tool reports honestly if 20KB was not reached.

Can I compress PNG to 20KB?

PNG is lossless, so photos rarely reach 20KB as PNG. Choose JPEG or WebP output for a much smaller file. Simple graphics may fit.

Why was my GIF, SVG or HEIC file rejected?

Animated GIF and WebP would lose their animation, SVG is a vector format where pixel compression does not apply, and HEIC cannot be reliably decoded in every browser. The tool rejects them with a message instead of silently changing them. Export a still JPG or PNG first.

Should I choose JPEG, WebP or PNG?

JPEG is the safest for forms and photos. WebP is often smaller but is not accepted everywhere. PNG is lossless and suited to graphics and screenshots, but photographs rarely reach small targets as PNG.

Quality

Does compression reduce image quality?

JPEG and WebP compression is lossy and removes detail; PNG does not but is usually larger. Keep your original file.

Why does my compressed image look smaller or softer?

To reach a tight target such as 20KB, the tool usually reduces the picture's dimensions and keeps a reasonable quality instead of using extreme compression, which causes blocky patches. You can tick Keep dimensions in Advanced settings to prefer the original size at lower quality.

Can I choose the exact pixel size?

You can set a maximum width and height in Advanced settings. The aspect ratio is preserved and the image is never enlarged, so the result fits inside your box. The tool does not crop or stretch to an exact shape.
